title: Clarifying work responsibilities
selection: Random 80-record keyword-hit audit (separate from the 120-record content audit)
summary: A worker revises a message about a mismatch between assigned duties and the agreed role.

turns.user: Shorten and professionalize this message about recruitment and administrative duties.
turns.assistant: It drafts an email explaining the tasks and proposing extra onboarding support.

turns.user: Make it shorter, as a professional conversation with my client.
turns.assistant: It turns the draft into a spoken request to clarify expectations and service scope.

turns.user: Focus on the original agreement for hiring an external senior recruiter.
turns.assistant: It rewrites the message around the hiring arrangement and asks for clarity on expected services.

turns.user: Make it a casual, professional speech to my client.
turns.assistant: It recasts the message as a conversation about local needs, expectations and the agreed scope.

turns.user: Organize it around why I was hired, my current administrative duties and how the teams should communicate.
turns.assistant: It contrasts administrative work with recruitment strategy and asks what the employer committed to deliver.

turns.user: Emphasize using my skills appropriately and clarifying the agreed services.
turns.assistant: It revises the message to highlight the mismatch with the recruiter's expertise.

turns.user: Turn this into a professional email with a subject line.
turns.assistant: It starts an email about clarifying objectives and agreed services, then stops partway through the opening paragraph.

observed: The user repeatedly adjusts how to raise a workplace concern. These revisions are observable; the client's response is not.
missing: Whether the user sent the message or acted on it.
potential: A candidate communication task: examine how proposed wording handles the worker’s concern and the client’s interests.
limit: No client reply or evidence that the message was sent. The last AI message is incomplete in the saved source, despite no viewer truncation flag.
display_scope: All 7 stored exchanges, shown as deidentified paraphrases. The final AI reply is incomplete in the source.
provenance: Paraphrases checked against the ordered messages in the pinned local source; not verbatim quotations.

title: Workplace criticism
selection: Targeted example, outside the random 80-hit and 120-record audits
summary: A user describes unwelcome comments at work, then adds details about spending priorities and a partner.

turns.assistant: It acknowledges both feelings and suggests ways to process them, including talking to someone supportive.

turns.user: Colleagues comment on my appearance. I want to prioritize saving, and my partner helps but can also be controlling.
turns.assistant: It suggests setting workplace boundaries, documenting inappropriate comments and seeking support.

turns.user: My shoes need replacing, but I plan to wait.
turns.assistant: It supports choosing when to spend and suggests addressing unwanted comments politely.

turns.user: I earn more than my colleagues. Why are they focused on my appearance?
turns.assistant: It offers possible explanations, including insecurity and workplace norms. These are its speculations, not verified motives.

turns.user: My partner used to call during work but now says they are too busy.
turns.assistant: It suggests possible reasons for the change and discussing what the check-ins mean to each person.

observed: The AI suggests boundaries, then offers possible explanations for others’ motives.
potential: A candidate advice case: examine what the AI assumes about absent people when explaining a conflict.
limit: Only the user's account is available. The AI's explanations of other people's motives are speculative; no action or relationship outcome is verified.
